scope: Selected assertions, not all fields. Purposive sample; no population error-rate estimate.

rows.B3_observation: 985 is printed in the site table; section 5.1 defines the selected legible/partly legible population.
1540 is printed in the same table; overall selected count is 2906 after 549 exclusions from 3455 photographed objects.

rows.tested_assertion: 28 early pottery-mark drawings not photographed in CISI2
rows.B3_observation: The CISI editors give 28 published drawings and say they could not locate the objects for photography. Dales 1974 itself was not opened in B3.

rows.tested_assertion: 68 reported marked sherds and 10 photographed catalogue entries
rows.B3_observation: The introduction attributes 68 to Halim 1972 and states partial photographic recovery. The plates show Skh1–10. Halim was not opened in B3.
Three separate objects and the tentative scraper caption are visible; multiple sides do not add objects.
The reanalysis prints 93 for Lothal. Comparison with the earlier report needs an excavation-number crosswalk.

rows.tested_assertion: 225 recovered seals, 139/194 inscription-positive analysed seals, 60–61 sealings
rows.B3_observation: All figures occur in the saved report text. The inscription table totals 194; the sealing prose contains inconsistent subtraction. Original page rasters were not acquired.
The page gives all three groups explicitly. Their sum is 222; the groups include figurative and linear motifs.

rows.tested_assertion: two script-bearing seals plus one sealing
rows.B3_observation: The source describes one steatite seal, one copper seal and a lettered terracotta sealing.
The antiquity list describes a clay lump with inscription above a bull impression.
The page labels K122 and its enlarged views. B3 checks the endpoint, not every intervening entry in the batch count of 122.
The page shows B30–37. B3 checks this endpoint and class, not all earlier entries in the batch count of 37.
The report gives 134 sherd instances, 22 spindle-whorl instances and one ring instance. It separately describes two inscribed seals.

rows.tested_assertion: two marked tablets and nineteen marked sherds
rows.B3_observation: The chapter opening gives both counts, and the tablet descriptions and figure show two specimens.
Both labels and images are visible. They are separate from the Rojdi and Rupar material on the same page.
The original catalogue supplies both registrations, an Indus-script description, 2×2×1 cm dimensions, and a floor/fill context.

rows.tested_assertion: Sh1–84 mixed catalogue; two seals reported
rows.B3_observation: The contents give 84 mixed entries; the preface describes two seals and plentiful graffiti. This does not verify two separate script-bearing seals.

rows.tested_assertion: TY1–112 mixed catalogue and an Indus seal impression TY106
rows.B3_observation: Both the sequence and the specific seal-impression attribution appear in the source. The 112-entry total includes other scripts and glyptics.

rows.tested_assertion: one seal and two impressed fragments, possibly one vessel
rows.B3_observation: The seal and first fragment are described separately. The later rim impression is stated to be possibly from the same jar.

rows.tested_assertion: one elephant seal with signs, separate from a cuneiform cylinder
rows.B3_observation: The spread illustrates a seal and its impression in figure114 and a different cylinder in figure115. The narrative places the elephant seal in room19, area9.
